title: Read open tab without navigation
user: I'm looking at a repo in the browser. Tell me the project name, roughly how many stars it has, and the latest commit subject—use the open tab only, don't navigate away or open new tabs.
observe: Calls closedai_app.state or embedded_browser read tools before answering
Does not navigate away from the repo URL
Answer cites plausible repo facts (stars, recent commit)
Completes without pausing the turn (no Escape / stop)

title: Open a docs URL in the embedded browser
user: Open https://example.com in the embedded browser next to this chat and confirm the main heading text once the page is ready.
observe: Uses embedded_browser or closedai_app browser_tab rather than OS open/xdg-open
Waits for load or idle before claiming the heading
Reports heading close to "Example Domain"

title: Orient from app state
user: Before changing anything: what folder is this chat working in, which model is selected here, and is the browser pane visible?
observe: Uses closedai_app.state (not guessing from memory)
Answers cwd/project path, model id, and browser visibility correctly
Does not mutate browser tabs or send spurious UI clicks

title: Runtime block vs closedai_app.state
user: Call closedai_app.state with workspace and chat sections. Compare callerPaneId, chat.provider, project.projectPath, workspace.appVersion, and chat.memory.chatMemoryIndexEnabled to the closedai.runtime block on this turn. Report match or mismatch in one short table. Do not edit files.
observe: Calls closedai_app.state before concluding
Values match closedai.runtime on the same turn (pane id, provider, projectPath, chatMemoryIndexEnabled via chat.memory)
Does not claim IDE-only or deny in-app MCP

title: Recall earlier text in this pane
user: In the first message of this eval only: write exactly: EVAL_RECALL_ANCHOR=violet-port-4400. Then in a follow-up turn (or if this is a continuation, skip writing it): use peer_chats.recall scope chat with query violet-port-4400 and quote the matching excerpt with item_id. No file edits.
observe: Uses peer_chats.recall with scope chat (not peer_chats.read on self)
Finds EVAL_RECALL_ANCHOR or violet-port-4400 when the anchor was sent earlier in this pane
Cites item_id from recall result

title: Search then recall drill-down
user: Use peer_chats.search with scope chat and a multi-word query taken from an earlier user message in this pane (pick distinctive words). For the top hit, call peer_chats.recall scope chat with that item_id and confirm the snippet matches. If search returns no hits, say so and fall back to recall with query. No file edits.
observe: Uses search(scope=chat) before or with recall
Drill-down via recall(item_id=...) when search hits
Honest fallback when index lags (indexPartial or empty hits)

title: First-time Stripe webhooks (human prompt)
user: I'm wiring up Stripe webhooks for the first time. From Stripe's official docs, what should I do in order—endpoints, signing secret, testing on my laptop, and which event types are worth handling first?
observe: Uses docs.stripe.com (embedded browser and/or search), not memory-only
Efficient path: site discovery or targeted doc reads before huge raw dumps
Ordered checklist with links; no unsolicited repo edits

title: Python.org current stable (human prompt)
user: What stable Python release should I download from python.org today? One paragraph with the version and where on the site you confirmed it.
observe: Confirms against python.org in the live session
Reasonable tool mix (discovery, navigate, or fetch)—not required to match a fixed recipe
No file edits in this workspace

title: GitHub OAuth first integration (complex)
user: I'm adding Sign in with GitHub to a web app for the first time. Using only GitHub's official documentation, give me a numbered checklist: register the OAuth app, callback URL rules, scopes for basic profile and email, and exchanging the authorization code on the server. Link each step to the doc page you actually used.
observe: Pulls from docs.github.com (or current official GitHub doc host), not generic blog posts
Multiple distinct doc pages or sections cited—not one paragraph from memory
Scopes and redirect/callback rules match what GitHub docs state
Web search alone is fine if it reaches the same official pages; shallow single-snippet answers fail
No unsolicited edits in the workspace chat cwd

title: Neon vs Supabase free tier (complex)
user: I'm choosing hosted Postgres for a side project. Compare Neon and Supabase using only what each vendor publishes on their own websites: free-tier storage and compute limits, connection or pooling limits, and whether branching or copy-on-write snapshots exist on free. Present as a short comparison table with links to each claim.
observe: Visits both neon.tech and supabase.com (or official doc subdomains), not roundup articles
At least four compared rows with vendor-specific links
Admits uncertainty when marketing pages are vague instead of inventing numbers
Efficient tool use: search and/or browser reads; no repo changes

title: Cloudflare Workers limits (complex)
user: We're planning to put a small HTTP API on Cloudflare Workers. From Cloudflare's official developer documentation, list the limits that usually bite new projects: request body size, CPU time per invocation, subrequest count, and any notes on WebSockets or long-running work. Each bullet should point to the doc page where you found it.
observe: Grounded in developers.cloudflare.com (or current Cloudflare docs), not forum guesses
Several limit categories with links—not a single generic overview paragraph
Numbers or caps quoted match the cited pages within reason
No file edits unless the user asked for code

title: Quick web lookup
user: What major Electron version shipped around August 2025? One sentence and a source link if you have one.
observe: Uses search.query or search.run—not embedded_browser navigate to Google
Single focused answer; no long essay
Mentions Electron 44 or cites a reasonable source from results
